title: pvVisItOpenFOAMReader
body:
## pvVisItOpenFOAMReader

Reads an OpenFOAM case through VisIt's OpenFOAM plugin (a variant of VTK's OpenFOAM reader): open the case's system/controlDict file. The output is a multiblock with the selected internal mesh, patches, zones and Lagrangian clouds, with fields over all time directories. Prefer foam (Schemaxis-curated, with checked defaults) or the native pvOpenFOAMReader, which handle decomposed cases and region selection; this reader is mainly a cross-check. One file supplies every time step the format stores.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The plugin's VisIt read options (for example decomposed versus reconstructed handling) cannot be changed here; use foam or pvOpenFOAMReader when you need them.
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrays and CellArrays: the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItOpenFOAMReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItOpenFOAMReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrays` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from OpenFOAM data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The OpenFOAM plugin offers the volume (cell) and point fields of the case; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | Path of the single OpenFOAM file to read (controlDict); the reader takes every time step the format stores from it. Use an absolute path; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Name the case's system/controlDict file. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Materials` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The OpenFOAM plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Meshes` | Names of the OpenFOAM meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The OpenFOAM plugin reports "internalMesh", the boundary patches, "Regions", cell, face and point zones, and Lagrangian clouds as separate meshes. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrays` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from OpenFOAM data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The OpenFOAM plugin offers the volume (cell) and point fields of the case; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItOpenFOAMReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
